column3: His soul or appetite is named rather than heart, and enjoyment is expressed as eating of the wealth.
His soul is not satisfied with good; the burial has no explicit adjective proper.
Darkness is repeated rather than varied with obscurity.
Not seeing and not knowing are expressed as completed actions.
He has not seen good, rather than expressly failing to enjoy prosperity.
The poor man walks before the living rather than the broader others.
Eyes is plural, and the first comparison is the sight of the eyes.
It is known that he is human, rather than that what happens to him is foreknown.
Many words increase futility; the wording does not separately repeat the more.
The days are numbered without an explicit few, and the life is described through futility.
